title: The HDB rate has a quarterly anchor. Bank loans need a closer look.
summary: A November starting point: the published HDB quarter, how SORA is reported, and the questions to take to your lender.

takeaways.text: CPF Ordinary Account: 2.50% p.a. for the same quarter.
SORA is a benchmark; MAS also publishes compounded tenors.

sections.heading: The published quarter
sections.text: CPF lists the HDB mortgage rate at 2.60% per annum for October–December 2026: the OA rate of 2.50% plus a 0.10 percentage-point administration fee. This is an existing quarterly publication, not a new November rate cut.

sections.heading: A different reference for bank loans
sections.text: MAS publishes overnight SORA and compounded one-, three- and six-month tenors. This briefing does not establish a current SORA fixing or a direction of travel.

sections.heading: What to do with this information
sections.text: Use the quarter as context, then compare the terms of an actual offer. Our editorial view: ask about the benchmark tenor, spread at each stage, fees and the date your commitment ends. A benchmark alone is insufficient to compare your total borrowing cost.
